item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Sharpen a Blurry Dog Photo

turns.text: This phone pic of my dog came out blurry. Can you make it clearer and bigger, 640 pixels on the long side? Keep it looking natural.

item.tests: Enhances a blurry supplied photo rather than replacing its subject or merely enlarging the blur.

answer_sheet.Enhancement style: Natural-looking blur reduction and sharpening, not a stylised remake.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: 640 pixels on the long side; preserve the original proportions and framing.
answer_sheet.Subject and background: Keep the same dog, pose, expression, and background.

must_haves: The same golden retriever from blurry-dog.jpg remains recognisable in the same pose.
The dog's visible contours and facial features are clearer than in the blurry source.
Fur and edges look natural, without pronounced sharpening halos or invented decorative detail.
The background and full original framing are preserved.
The delivered image has a 640-pixel long edge and preserves the source aspect ratio.

turns.text: This pic of my dog came out blurry when I took it on my phone. I was a little disappointed because I really like this photo. Could you make it clearer and bigger, with 640 pixels on the long side? I’m fond of this dog, so even an ordinary photo like this means a lot to me. Please keep it looking natural.

dialog.agent:
I couldn't sharpen your dog's photo. Magic Hour turned down the request because your account doesn't have enough credits, so nothing was made and there's no download link.

The plan was a free-plan edit (the flux-2-klein model, about 5 credits) that only sharpens the fur, eyes and background. I told it to keep the same dog, pose, colours and lighting and not to over-sharpen, so the photo stays natural. If you top up your credits or wait for your free credits to refresh, I can run that same request again.

Before then, please check the size you want. The photo you attached looks like it's already 1024×1024 pixels. If so, 640 pixels on the long side would make it smaller, not bigger. It could be one of these:
- **Clearer at 640 px**, as you asked, which would shrink it slightly.
- **Clearer and actually bigger**, by sharpening it and then doubling its size with Magic Hour's upscaler. That would cost more credits.

Tell me which one you'd like.
dialog.why: The reply explains that the edit failed for lack of credits, then ends by asking the user to choose between two size options and waits for their answer.
dialog.user: Let's go with clearer at 640 pixels on the long side, like I asked, even if that means it shrinks a bit. I didn't realise it was already that big, so I suppose I just assumed a blurry phone photo would be small. Please keep the original proportions and framing, and don't add any text to it. I'll sort out the credits and get back to you so you can run it again.

dialog.agent:
Sounds good. Once your credits are sorted, I'll run it with these settings:

- **Sharper and clearer:** crisp fur, eyes, nose and tongue, and a clearer background. It should still look like a natural phone photo, not over-sharpened or painted.
- **640 pixels on the long side.** If the original is 1024×1024, the result will be 640×640.
- **Same proportions and framing:** nothing cropped or moved, and the same pose, colours and lighting.
- **No text** or anything else added to the photo.

It should cost about 5 credits. When you're ready, just say "go ahead" and I'll run it and send you the download link. If you change your mind and want it bigger instead, that's an option too.
dialog.why: It lays out the settings and the roughly 5-credit cost, then waits for the user to say "go ahead" before running the job.
dialog.user: Yes, that all looks right, so go ahead once the credits are sorted. Please keep the same dog, pose, expression and background exactly as they are, since that's what makes the photo special to me. I'm happy with 640×640 and don't need it bigger. My only worry is that it ends up looking too sharp or fake, so natural is definitely better than perfect.

dialog.agent:
I'll wait until you tell me your credits are sorted before running it.

Here's what the request will include:

- **The same dog, pose, expression and background.** The tool is only meant to make the existing photo clearer, not change what's in it.
- **A gentle, natural result:** the photo shouldn't look too sharp, glossy, painted or fake. If there's a choice, it should look natural rather than perfect.
- **640×640**, with the same framing and no text.

This kind of AI editing can still change small details on its own, like the shape of a marking or a few blades of grass. When it's done, compare it with your original. If anything looks off, I can run it again with a gentler setting.

Just say "credits are sorted" and I'll run it and send you the download link.
dialog.why: It is waiting for the user to confirm that credits are sorted before it runs the edit, which is a confirmation to proceed.
dialog.user: Credits are sorted, so please go ahead and run it. Thanks for the heads-up about small details changing; I'll compare it closely with the original blurry-dog.jpg when it's done. I know every marking on this dog by heart, so I'll spot it right away if anything looks off.

turns.agent:
I ran it, but Magic Hour turned it down again because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was made, so there's no download link yet.

This edit needs about 5 credits, so your account must have fewer than that available right now. A few possible reasons:
- A purchase or top-up hasn't finished going through yet. Sometimes it takes a few minutes.
- The credits went to a different Magic Hour account than the one connected here.
- Free-plan credits haven't refreshed yet.

You could check your balance on the Magic Hour website under the same login. Once it shows at least 5 credits, tell me and I'll run it again with the same settings: 640×640, the same dog, pose, expression, markings and background, no text, and a gentle, natural look.

timeline.text:
The user wants it clearer and bigger, with 640 pixels on the long side. The image appears to be 1024x1024, which would make 640 smaller, so the request and the dimensions don't quite line up. I'm weighing an upscale_image at 2x, which the free plan allows, though that would give an output twice the original size.

I'm weighing whether 640px even makes sense here, since the image looks like 1024x1024 and that would shrink it rather than enlarge it. An edit at 640px would keep the dimensions exact and sharpen the image, though a generative pass could alter the dog, so an upscale that preserves the original might be the more faithful route. I'll go ahead with the cheap 640px edit and mention the mismatch in the answer.
